members: Olanzapine: Pines family, most severe metabolic risk and weight gain (Dulcan p.823, StahlNeuro p.196)
Quetiapine: Pines family, 3-tier dose mechanism (25-100mg H1 hypnotic, 300mg NET antidepressant in adults, 400-800mg D2/5-HT2A antipsychotic) (StahlNeuro p.218-219)
Risperidone: Dones family, potent D2/5-HT2A antagonism with dose-dependent EPS and marked prolactin elevation (Dulcan p.821, p.825, StahlNeuro p.221)
Paliperidone: Dones family, active metabolite 9-OH-risperidone, predominantly renal elimination with <10% hepatic metabolism (Dulcan p.786, StahlNeuro p.232)
drug_class.mechanism: 5-HT2A antagonism > D2 antagonism (SDA) releasing dopamine in nigrostriatal/mesocortical pathways; H1, 5-HT2C, M1, alpha1 receptor blockade (StahlNeuro p.184, p.204)
kinetics: Olanzapine: t1/2 ~30h, CYP1A2 substrate (induced by smoking) (Dulcan p.786-787, StahlKids p.351)
Quetiapine: t1/2 6-7h, CYP3A4 substrate to active metabolite Norquetiapine (Dulcan p.786-787, StahlNeuro p.218)
Risperidone: t1/2 3h, CYP2D6 substrate to 9-OH-risperidone (Dulcan p.786-787, StahlKids p.423)
Paliperidone: t1/2 ~23h, <10% first-pass hepatic clearance, renal excretion (Dulcan p.785-786, StahlNeuro p.232)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: 1-2 weeks for initial response; 4-6 weeks for full trial (Dulcan p.402, p.797, StahlKids p.355)

items: Schizophrenia (EOS): FDA approved for 13+ (Olanzapine, Quetiapine, Risperidone) and 12+ (Paliperidone OROS) (Dulcan p.402, p.787)
Bipolar I Mania: FDA approved for ages 10-17 (Quetiapine, Risperidone) and 13-17 (Olanzapine) (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.351)
Bipolar Depression: Symbyax (Olanzapine + Fluoxetine) FDA approved for 10-17; Quetiapine failed RCTs in pediatric bipolar depression (Dulcan p.301, p.805)
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Irritability: Risperidone FDA approved for ages 5-16 (Dulcan p.787, p.809)
key_numbers: NNT = 3-13 for SGA response in early-onset schizophrenia (Dulcan p.796)
NNT = 3-6 for SGA response/remission in pediatric bipolar mania (Dulcan p.805)
NNT = 2-5 for Risperidone in ASD irritability (Dulcan p.809)
NNT = 3-6 for Clozapine in treatment-resistant EOS (Dulcan p.397, p.796)

items: Metabolic dysfunction & weight gain: Olanzapine highest risk, followed by Risperidone/Paliperidone and Quetiapine (Dulcan p.823-824, StahlNeuro p.196)
Extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) & Akathisia: Dose-dependent with Risperidone (>2-3mg/day) and Paliperidone; lowest with Quetiapine (Dulcan p.821, StahlNeuro p.221)
Hyperprolactinemia: Severe/sustained with Paliperidone >= Risperidone; minimal with Quetiapine (Dulcan p.825)
Sedation & hepatic transaminase elevation: Olanzapine causes ALT elevation in 48% of youth (Dulcan p.825-826)
key_numbers: NNH = 3 for >=7% weight gain with Olanzapine in youth (Dulcan p.823)
NNH = 6 for >=7% weight gain with Risperidone (Dulcan p.823)
NNH = 9 for >=7% weight gain with Quetiapine (Dulcan p.823)
NNH = 3-5 for ALT elevation >3x ULN with Olanzapine (Dulcan p.825-826)
48% ALT elevation rate with Olanzapine in pediatric schizophrenia (Dulcan p.825-826)

items: Neuromotor monitoring: SAS (parkinsonism), BARS (akathisia), AIMS (tardive dyskinesia) at baseline, 3 months, annually (Dulcan p.827 Table 37-7)
Cardiac ECG monitoring: Recommended at baseline for Ziprasidone (+8.74 msec QTc) and Clozapine; required for cardiac risk history (Dulcan p.824-825, p.827)
QTc threshold for discontinuation: QTc >= 500 msec requires immediate antipsychotic discontinuation (Dulcan p.832)
key_numbers: QTc < 440 msec normal in children (Dulcan p.825, p.832)
QTc >= 500 msec critical discontinuation threshold (Dulcan p.832)
3 hours post-injection observation for Olanzapine Relprevv due to PDSS (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.355)

items: Olanzapine: Starting 2.5-5mg/day at bedtime, target 10mg/day, max 20mg/day; smoking reduces levels by 40-50% via CYP1A2 (Dulcan p.786-787, StahlKids p.355-356)
Quetiapine: Starting 25mg bid (IR) or 50mg/day (XR), target 400-800mg/day; XR tablets swallowed whole (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.412)
Risperidone: Starting 0.25-0.5mg/day, target 1-3mg/day; no added efficacy above 3mg/day with increased EPS (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.425, p.428)
Paliperidone: OROS 3-12mg/day; swallow whole (never crush/chew) to prevent dose dumping; adjust for renal impairment (Dulcan p.787, StahlKids p.370, p.376-377)
key_numbers: 3 mg/day efficacy ceiling for Risperidone in pediatric schizophrenia/mania (StahlKids p.425, p.428)
40-50% decrease in Olanzapine levels from smoking (Dulcan p.786, StahlKids p.356)
CrCl < 50 mL/min requires Paliperidone dose reduction (max 6mg/day CrCl 50-80, max 3mg/day CrCl 10-50) (StahlKids p.376)

items: BMI percentile & z-score measured at baseline, every visit, 3 months, 6 months, annually (Dulcan p.827 Table 37-7)
Fasting glucose/HbA1c & lipids measured at baseline, 3 months, 6 months, annually (Dulcan p.827 Table 37-7)
Critical intervention threshold: >5% body weight gain in 3 months or >0.5 increase in BMI z-score (Dulcan p.829, p.834)
Intervention algorithm: Lifestyle -> Switch to low metabolic SGA -> Add Metformin 500-1000mg BID (Dulcan p.833-835)
key_numbers: BMI percentile >= 85th-95th = overweight; >= 95th = obesity (Dulcan p.829, DSM p.377)
HOMA-IR >= 4.4 indicates severe insulin resistance in adolescents (Dulcan p.829-830)
Triglycerides/HDL ratio > 3.5 indicates insulin resistance (Dulcan p.829-830)
Fasting triglycerides >= 110 mg/dL, Fasting glucose >= 126 mg/dL (diabetes) (Dulcan p.829)

items: Prolactin elevation rank order: Paliperidone >= Risperidone > Haloperidol > Olanzapine > Ziprasidone > Quetiapine >= Clozapine > Aripiprazole (Dulcan p.825)
Clinical presentation: Amenorrhea, galactorrhea, gynecomastia, delayed puberty, osteopenia (Dulcan p.825, StahlKids p.368)
Symptomatic testing protocol: Morning fasting blood sample 8-12h post-dose (Dulcan p.830)
Management: Prolactin > 200 ng/mL requires pituitary MRI; < 200 ng/mL add Aripiprazole 5-15mg/day or switch SGA (Dulcan p.833, p.835-836)
key_numbers: 200 ng/mL prolactin threshold requiring pituitary MRI scan (Dulcan p.835-836)
5-15 mg/day low-dose Aripiprazole add-on to normalize prolactin (Dulcan p.833, p.836)

high_yield: Olanzapine carries the highest metabolic risk (NNH = 3 for >=7% weight gain) and causes ALT elevation in 48% of youth (Dulcan p.823-826, StahlNeuro p.196)
Quetiapine acts as 3 distinct drugs: 25-100mg H1 hypnotic, 300mg NET antidepressant (in adults), and 400-800mg D2/5-HT2A antipsychotic/antimanic (StahlNeuro p.218-219)
Quetiapine failed in RCTs for pediatric bipolar depression; Symbyax and Lurasidone are the only FDA-approved treatments for pediatric bipolar depression (Dulcan p.301, p.805, StahlKids p.418)
Risperidone shows dose-dependent EPS above 2-3mg/day and has a clinical efficacy ceiling at 3mg/day in pediatric schizophrenia/mania (Dulcan p.821, StahlKids p.425, p.428)
Risperidone and Paliperidone cause the most severe hyperprolactinemia (Paliperidone >= Risperidone) leading to galactorrhea, gynecomastia, and bone loss (Dulcan p.825, StahlKids p.367, p.423)
Paliperidone is excreted renally (<10% hepatic clearance) with zero CYP450 drug interactions; OROS tablets must never be crushed or chewed (Dulcan p.786, StahlNeuro p.232, StahlKids p.377)
TEOSS study showed equal efficacy between Olanzapine, Risperidone, and Molindone (34-50%), but Olanzapine caused the most weight gain (Dulcan p.402, p.821)
HOMA-IR >= 4.4 or Triglycerides/HDL ratio > 3.5 indicates marked insulin resistance in adolescents (Dulcan p.829-830)
IMPACT trial proved adding Metformin (500-1000mg BID) is as effective as switching to a low metabolic SGA (Dulcan p.824, p.835)
Symptomatic hyperprolactinemia > 200 ng/mL requires pituitary MRI; adjunctive low-dose Aripiprazole (5-15mg/day) effectively normalizes prolactin (Dulcan p.833, p.835-836)
